title: A Green Forest Instead of a Hospital Ward: How VR Is Leaving the Game Arcade
title_zh: 病房变成绿色森林：虚拟现实正走出游戏厅
intro_zh: 本文约 539 词，共 8 个自然段，包含 6 个 CET-4 核心词（simulate、equipment、treatment、realistic、immerse、afford），句子难度中等，适合四级阅读训练。

paragraphs.en: At a rehabilitation centre in Shanghai, a young man who has not walked for months puts on a headset. Instead of a white ward, he sees a green forest path with birds overhead. He lifts one foot, then the other, and slowly follows the road. His doctor says the game takes his mind off the pain, and every week he walks a little further.
paragraphs.zh: 在上海的一家康复中心，一个几个月没能走路的年轻人戴上了头戴设备。他看到的不是白色的病房，而是一条头顶有飞鸟的绿色林间小路。他抬起一只脚，再抬起另一只，慢慢沿着路走。他的医生说，这个游戏让他忘记疼痛，因此每周他都能多走一点。

paragraphs.en: This is virtual reality, or VR, at work. The idea behind it is simple. A computer builds a world that does not exist, and a headset places your eyes and ears inside that world. Good systems do far more than show pictures. They simulate movement, sound and even touch, so the brain reacts as if the scene were really happening. The equipment is no longer science fiction either. In many shopping malls, a basic headset costs less than a mid-range smartphone, and it fits in a small bag.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是正在投入使用的虚拟现实（VR）。它的原理很简单：计算机建造一个并不存在的世界，头戴设备把你的眼睛和耳朵放进那个世界里。好的系统远不只是给你看画面：它们模拟运动、声音甚至触觉，让大脑的反应就好像场景真的在发生一样。相关设备也不再是科幻小说里的东西了。在许多商场，一套基础头戴设备比一部中档智能手机还便宜，而且能装进一个小包里。

paragraphs.en: Medicine may be the most surprising user. In several hospitals in Beijing and Guangzhou, doctors now offer VR as pain treatment during small operations and blood tests. Because the young patient is busy watching a realistic cartoon ocean, the brain pays less attention to the needle. Researchers at a Canadian university found that children using VR reported noticeably less pain, and their parents said the visit felt calmer.
paragraphs.zh: 医疗也许是最令人意外的应用领域。在北京和广州的几家医院里，医生现在把小手术和抽血时的疼痛治疗交给 VR 来完成。因为小患者正忙着看一段逼真的卡通海洋，大脑对针头的注意力就减少了。加拿大一所大学的研究人员发现，使用 VR 的孩子报告说疼痛明显减轻了，他们的父母也表示就诊过程安静了许多。

paragraphs.en: Training is another big area. Firefighters can practise entering a burning building without breathing any smoke. Medical students repeat a difficult operation twenty times before they touch a real person. A railway company in Germany trains its drivers the same way. Mistakes in a virtual world cost nothing, and nobody gets hurt. Trainees also dare to ask questions they might avoid in a real emergency.
paragraphs.zh: 培训是另一个重要领域。消防员可以在不吸入任何烟雾的情况下练习进入着火建筑；医学生可以在真正接触病人之前把一台高难度手术重复二十遍；德国一家铁路公司也用同样的方式培训司机。在虚拟世界里犯错不花一分钱，也不会有人受伤。受训者还敢提出一些在真实紧急情况下他们可能会回避的问题。

paragraphs.en: Schools are joining in too. In a history lesson, a class in Chengdu can immerse itself in a street of ancient Rome, walking past markets and temples, hearing shopkeepers argue about prices. Teachers report that students remember far more than they do from a page of text. 'I felt as if I had really been there,' one girl wrote in her notebook, 'so the facts stopped being strange names.'
paragraphs.zh: 学校也在加入进来。在一堂历史课上，成都的一个班级可以让自己沉浸在古罗马的街道中：走过集市和神庙，听店主为价格争吵。老师们反映，学生记住的东西远比读一页文字要多。一个女孩在笔记本上写道：“我觉得自己真的去过那里，所以那些史实不再只是些陌生的名字了。”

paragraphs.en: Price, of course, decides who gets to try. Five years ago a professional headset cost thousands of dollars and needed a powerful computer beside it. Today a family that can afford a new laptop can usually buy a simple headset as well. Schools and public libraries in many Chinese cities now lend them out for a week, the way they lend books, so a curious child can test one at home.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，价格决定了谁能尝试。五年前，一台专业头戴设备要花上千美元，旁边还得配一台性能强大的电脑。如今，买得起一台新笔记本电脑的家庭通常也买得起一台简易头戴设备。中国许多城市的学校和公共图书馆现在会像借书一样把它外借一周，于是一个好奇的孩子也能在家里试一试。

paragraphs.en: VR is not perfect, though. Using a headset for a long time still makes some people feel sick, and few families really want a heavy machine in the living room. Experts also remind us that a virtual forest is no substitute for a real walk in the park with friends.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，VR 并不完美。长时间戴头戴设备仍会让一些人感到不适，而且很少有家庭真的愿意在客厅里摆一台沉重的机器。专家还提醒我们，虚拟的森林代替不了和朋友在公园里的真实散步。

paragraphs.en: Still, the direction is clear. The technology is moving out of game arcades and into hospitals, classrooms and training halls, where it saves money, reduces fear and helps people learn faster. In a few years, putting on a headset may feel as ordinary as putting on a pair of glasses — a tool for practising and healing, not simply an escape from the real world.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管如此，方向是清楚的。这项技术正从游戏厅走进医院、教室和训练大厅，在那里它省钱、减少恐惧，并帮助人们学得更快。再过几年，戴上头戴设备也许就像戴上一副眼镜一样平常——它是一种用于练习和治疗的工具，而不只是逃离现实的方式。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why VR headsets have become popular among teenage gamers.
How VR is now being used in practical fields such as medicine, training and education.
The complete history of virtual reality since the 1990s.
Why schools should stop students from using VR headsets.
questions.explain: 全文从康复中心的场景切入，依次介绍 VR 在医疗止痛、职业培训、课堂教学和普及价格方面的应用，主旨是“VR 正进入实际领域”，故选 B。A、C、D 均非文章重点，文中也未提及学校禁用。

questions.q: According to the passage, why do children feel less pain when using VR during a blood test?
options: They are given more medicine before the test.
They are allowed to close their eyes during the test.
Their attention is drawn to something interesting, so the brain notices the needle less.
The test is finished much faster than usual.
questions.explain: 第三段明确指出，孩子忙着看逼真的卡通海洋，大脑对针头的注意力就减少了，因此疼痛感降低，与 C 一致。文中说用药更少而非更多，A 错；B、D 属无中生有。

questions.q: What can be inferred from the last two paragraphs?
options: VR will soon replace real walks in the park.
VR is a useful tool, but it still has its weaknesses.
No family will ever use a headset at home.
Headsets are too expensive for any ordinary family.
questions.explain: 倒数第二段指出长时间使用会让人不适、设备笨重，虚拟森林也不能代替真实散步；最后一段又说它省钱、减轻恐惧、帮助学习，可见 VR 有用但有局限，选 B。A、C、D 都与原文相反或过于绝对。

questions.q: The word 'afford' in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: afford 意为“买得起、负担得起”，与 have enough money for 最接近。该段讲价格下降后普通家庭也能买得起简易头戴设备，可见重点在“付得起钱”，故选 A；B、C、D 均与词义不符。
